decisive_items: cystic background with “dirty” necrosis and pseudopapillary clusters of moderately atypical cells with cyanophilic cytoplasm
salivary duct carcinoma was initially considered
homogeneously enhancing nodular lesion in the superficial lobe of the right parotid gland, surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule
response.rationale: Cystic lesion with dirty necrosis and pseudopapillary clusters of moderately atypical cells favors mucoepidermoid carcinoma, the most common malignant parotid tumor; the thin capsule and lack of nodal disease suggest a lower-grade lesion. Salivary duct carcinoma was only 'initially considered' and typically shows more solid growth and comedonecrosis.

rejected.why: Initial consideration is not definitive; cytology lacks classic ductal features and CT shows a well-capsulated lesion more consistent with low-grade malignancy.
Warthin tumor is benign and typically shows oncocytic cells with lymphoid stroma; cytology here is suspicious for malignancy.
Pleomorphic adenoma is benign and would not show dirty necrosis or atypical pseudopapillary clusters; cytology contradicts this.
